result.topic_en: Riemann takes the Mellin transform of the series for 2K/π (Jacobi's formula for the sum of two squares, with q = e^{-πx}) and expresses it as Γ(s)π^{-s} times ζ(s)(1−2^{-s}) and an L-series product (an Euler product over primes), in effect ζ(s)L(s,χ_4).
result.transcription:
$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-\pi}$ [?]

$\frac{2K}{\pi} = 1 + \frac{4q}{1+q^2} + \frac{4q^2}{1+q^4} + \frac{4q^3}{1+q^6}$
$q = e^{-\pi x}$
$\int_0^\infty \left(\frac{2K}{\pi} - 1\right) x^{s-1}\,\partial x = 4\Sigma \int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-n\pi x}}{e^{2n\pi x}+1}\, x^{s-1}\,\partial x$
$= 4 \int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-\pi x}}{e^{2\pi x}+1}\, x^{s-1}\,\partial x$ [-$\Sigma n^{-s}$-] [?]
$= 4\, \Pi(s-1)\, \pi^{-s}$ [-$(\Sigma \ldots)^2$-] [-$\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2^s}}$-] $\left(1-\frac{1}{2^s}\right)$ $\Pi \frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{p^s}}$ $\Pi\left(1-(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}} p^{-s}\right)$ [?]

methods.what: Series expansion of the complete elliptic integral 2K/π as a Lambert-type series in the nome q (Jacobi), with q = e^{-πx}
Mellin transform of (2K/π − 1), computed by termwise integration of the series

methods.what: Expression of the Mellin transform as Γ(s)π^{-s} times Euler products: ζ(s)(1−2^{-s}) times a Dirichlet L-function with the character (−1)^{(p−1)/2}
